parts: Please read/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/24_GNP_BB_CONTINUATION_AFTER_LOCAL_MOMENT_SCREEN_20261113.md, and summarize the status of the research so far?
I’ll read the continuation note and the project’s result and caution summaries, then summarize what is established and what remains open.

The continuation note and live register agree: the latest work proves useful average bounds for the remaining tail, but the bound needed at every individual height is still open. The strongest accepted width remains \(567/1000\); the proposed improvement to \(9/16\) is conditional.

**The research has achieved a narrower zero enclosure at large heights and quantitative control of the remaining tail on average. The central unresolved step is control at every individual height.** As of [Note24](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/24_GNP_BB_CONTINUATION_AFTER_LOCAL_MOMENT_SCREEN_20261113.md), B05 and E09/E10 are complete; B06 is prepared but unstarted.

1. **The strongest acquired zero bound is \(567/1000=0.567\).**  
   For some positive, unevaluated \(t_*\), every zero \(x+iy\) of the Newman heat-flow function satisfies
   \[
   |y|<0.567
   \quad\text{when}\quad
   0<t\le t_*,\qquad |x|\ge4\pi e^{1/t}.
   \]
   This improves the earlier \(4/7\) bound by \(31/7000\). It holds both along the prescribed height-dependent heat curve and throughout the stated exterior region at each fixed time. It does **not** cover all heights or time zero. [Accepted result](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/11_newman_heat_flow_reductions_and_certificates.md:26)

2. **The latest work isolates and controls the difficult arithmetic tail on average.**  
   The quantity \(Q(X)\) is a Poisson-weighted squared norm of an oscillatory finite sum. E09 reduces it to a middle band, with uniformly vanishing discarded error, and proves
   \[
   \frac1U\int_U^{2U}Q(X)\,dX=O(U^{-25/1024}).
   \]
   It also proves vanishing averages on sufficiently long shorter windows. Consequently, heights where \(Q\) exceeds any fixed positive threshold occupy a vanishing proportion. A specified family of whole-interval resonator weights likewise cannot produce a persistent positive average. **Exceptional individual heights remain possible under these results.** [Proof and review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/reviews/09_GNP_BB_E09_ADDITIONAL_AGENT_REVIEW_20261113.md)

3. **The proposed improvement to \(9/16=0.5625\) remains conditional.**  
   The Green-potential argument would deliver that width along the heat curve if
   \[
   Q(X)\le\frac4{66^2}
   \]
   at every sufficiently large center. That inequality is **neither proved nor disproved**. Small averages do not establish it, and a growing upper allowance does not establish a counterexample. The remaining problem is cancellation in the middle-band sum at actual individual heights. [Conditional reduction](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/15_GNP_BB_B04_SIGNED_GREEN_ACQUISITION_20261113.md)

4. **B06 will test a specific possible obstruction to that sufficient bound.**  
   It proposes an adaptively centered triangular average at scale \(H=U^{1/32}\), seeking a value at least \(5/66^2\) at arbitrarily large heights. Such a witness would violate the chosen sufficient budget somewhere in its window. It would not establish a nonreal zero or invalidate every Green-potential approach. The existing averaging theorem does not settle this shorter-window question. [B06 specification](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/research-progress/handoffs/GNP-BB-B06-r1.md)

The compact-height region, passage toward time zero, global Newman conclusions, and repeated contraction toward the real axis remain open. The completed results are recorded as **proved in-note from named inputs, with internal additional-agent acceptance**; they have no independent specialist review. Those qualifications follow the [results index](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/README.md) and the [avoid index](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/README.md), particularly its [rule against broadening scoped exclusions](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/07_scoped_exclusions_read_as_universal.md).
Ok, please continue with B06

I’ll start B06 with the fixed short-window test, keeping its scale and threshold unchanged. I’ll first check the transfer errors, then test whether the actual arithmetic phases can support the proposed lower bound.

The fixed window is shorter than the range where the existing average bound tends to zero. I’m checking the moving cutoffs and phase errors first, so that any resonance argument applies to the actual moment rather than just a frozen approximation.

I found an actual-height construction where a short block of terms stays almost perfectly aligned across the prescribed window. Its total contribution appears to decay too quickly to reach the fixed threshold. I’m checking its interaction with all remaining terms before treating that as a failure of the proposed mechanism.

The interaction check also gives a vanishing bound: this aligned block cannot add a fixed surplus even when all its cross terms are included. A broader estimate shows the same limitation for a small collection of frequency blocks. That leaves the full B06 witness open; I’m recording the precise scope and checking the proof and arithmetic.

**B06 is complete with a scoped negative result: the tested resonance mechanism is too weak.**

I constructed a block of terms whose phases align at actual heights throughout the prescribed short window. However:

- Its squared norm decays like \(U^{-241/640}\).
- Its effect on the **complete moment**, including interaction with every remaining term, is only \(O(U^{-59/320})\).

Thus this aligned block cannot supply the fixed surplus sought by B06. The proof also limits broader sparse collections of such blocks. The moving cutoffs, weights and phase-freezing errors are accounted for in [Note25](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/25_GNP_BB_B06_SHORT_WINDOW_AND_ACTUAL_PACKET_20261113.md).

**The full short-window witness remains open**, as does the every-center \(4/66^2\) bound. The accepted width stays \(567/1000\).

The argument has same-assistant checking and passed its exact arithmetic and document checks; separate review is pending. I updated the research register and saved the [continuation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/26_GNP_BB_CONTINUATION_AFTER_SHORT_PACKET_TEST_20261113.md).

**Next: [E] GNP-BB-E11 — Sol / ultra**, for a distinct analytical review of this fixed result.
Do you think that this approach is showing promise? What are some of the blockers?
I’ll assess the approach against the results so far, separating the progress in large-height bounds from what would be needed for a global result.

A further blocker is the normalization: on the current heat schedule, its uniform nonvanishing bound deteriorates as the width approaches \(1/2\). Even a successful \(9/16\) estimate would therefore leave a separate obstacle to continued contraction toward the real axis.

**I see moderate promise for stronger large-height estimates. Its promise as a route to RH is still unestablished.**

There is substantive progress: the acquired width improved from \(4/7\) to \(0.567\), the argument was extended to a common-time exterior, and the remaining arithmetic tail now has quantitative average bounds. Those are concrete gains recorded in the [results index](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/README.md) and [heat-flow summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/11_newman_heat_flow_reductions_and_certificates.md). B05 and B06 mainly clarified which mechanisms are insufficient; they did not improve the width further.

The principal blockers are:

1. **Average control versus control at every height.**  
   This is the immediate mathematical gap. A moment can be small almost everywhere while retaining rare large spikes. The Green argument needs the required bound at *every* sufficiently large center. A smaller exceptional proportion does not exclude an exception precisely where it matters.

2. **The difficult cancellation involves the complete arithmetic sum.**  
   Taking absolute values loses too much. B06 shows that aligning a small block—even at actual heights—can produce too little mass to matter. A successful argument needs control involving many more terms and their interactions. B06 was also a stress test of the proposed sufficient bound: failing to break that bound does not establish it. This is exactly the distinction emphasized by the [avoid index](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/README.md) and its [scoped-exclusion rule](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/07_scoped_exclusions_read_as_universal.md).

3. **The current normalization encounters another obstacle near width \(1/2\).**  
   On the chosen heat schedule, the comparison factor’s argument satisfies approximately
   \[
   \Re s=\frac34+\frac y2.
   \]
   Its elementary nonvanishing estimate relies on staying uniformly above \(\Re s=1\). That margin disappears as \(y\) approaches \(1/2\). Thus even obtaining \(9/16\) would leave a separate obstacle to repeated contraction toward zero. This limitation is already identified in [Note14](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/notes/14_GNP_BB_B04_BROADER_PAIR_COMPARISON_20261113.md); the underlying Euler-product domain is stated in [DLMF](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.2.E11).

4. **The controlled region retreats to infinity as time approaches zero.**  
   The exterior begins at \(|x|\ge4\pi e^{1/t}\). Consequently, the theorem supplies no direct time-zero limit at a fixed height. The missing interior and intermediate-time region require separate estimates, and the current onsets remain unevaluated. The published global criterion explicitly requires those additional pieces. [Polymath, Proposition 3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.12438v2#S3)

My recommendation is to finish E11’s distinct review, then judge further work by whether it closes one of these gaps. **An every-center estimate with a usable strict margin would increase my confidence substantially.** Another representation, average-decay improvement, or isolated alignment would need a demonstrated connection to that goal.

I saved this judgment and its qualifications in the [strategic assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/02_height_time_boundary_bootstrap/reviews/STRATEGIC_STATUS_AND_BLOCKERS_20261113.md).

I’ll complete E11’s analytical review first, then build a manuscript that develops the accepted results in a single chain of arguments. I’ll keep numerical checks as supporting evidence, make the remaining gaps explicit, and place the PDF outside the repository.

The E11 analytical check has found no correction needed so far. The manuscript will distinguish the proved \(0.567\) exterior width from the conditional \(9/16\) Green-potential step, then explain what the average bounds and packet results establish about the remaining obstacle.

The central distinction is now clear: the method gives a uniform exterior zero enclosure, while the proposed deeper step needs a bound at every center. The later results show that long averages become small and sparse aligned packets have a vanishing effect, but they leave exceptional centers unresolved. I’m organizing the proofs around that distinction.

I’ve traced the main claims back to their proof notes and checked how they depend on one another. The manuscript will include the full error accounting—from the corrected Riemann–Siegel expansion through the finite sums and Green inequality—so the proved results and the still-unproved premise can be assessed together.

E11 is complete and accepts all eleven estimates without mathematical correction. This is a distinct-agent internal review using the stated inputs. I’m now writing the manuscript, including the reviewed distinction between a packet’s own energy and its effect on the complete moment.

The exterior-width proof is drafted, including the finite-window argument and its overlap with the published far-tail theorem. The next sections develop the Green comparison and the local moment estimates, with separate notation for strip height and averaging-window length.

The mean-value proofs now account explicitly for moving cutoffs, nearby frequencies, and exact product coincidences. The short-window section will then show why the quartic packet really aligns at actual heights, yet its contribution remains too small even after including its interaction with the rest of the sum.

The full draft is written, and its final section states the outstanding arithmetic, carrier, compact-height, and time-propagation tasks. I’m now checking the assembled manuscript for mathematical consistency and layout, with the PDF and all build products outside the repository.

The manuscript compiles cleanly, with no unresolved references or layout warnings. I’m checking the rendered pages and updating the research records so they point to the completed E11 review and the new manuscript.

The 30-page manuscript has passed the page checks, and the PDF is saved in the external research archive. I’m finishing the build record and research-status links. The main conclusion remains unchanged: the \(0.567\) exterior width is proved from the named inputs; the every-center moment bound and global/time-zero extensions remain open.

E11 is complete: the distinct reviewer accepted the estimates without mathematical correction.
